memos.headline: S07 leads on momentum; S01 and S03 in technical downtrends worth avoiding
memos.body: As of 2025-10-10, the universe is broadly pulling back on a 1-week basis, but the dispersion in intermediate trends is wide. I have highest conviction in S07, which sits just 2.2% off its 52-week high, is +10.8% above its 50-day mean, and shows dominant relative strength vs SPY of +14.5% over 4 weeks and +13.5% over 12 weeks—classic leadership. S08 is a secondary favorite with +12.8% 12-week relative strength and only a 5.3% drawdown, though the sharp -4.9% weekly pullback warrants watching the 50-day area (~237) for support. On the other side, S01 is the weakest name: RSI 35.7, trading 7.6% below its 200-day mean, down 16.7% from highs, and bleeding relative strength at -7.8% over 12 weeks—a clear avoid until it reclaims its 200-day. S03 shares similar weakness with RSI 40.1, -4.1% below its 50-day, and -7.3% 12-week relative strength, making it another avoid until it can hold above ~225.

views.note: Strongest relative strength in the universe (+14.5% 4w vs SPY), only -2.2% from highs, RSI 65 not yet overbought; would reassess on a close below the 50-day (~443).
Solid uptrend with +12.8% 12w relative strength and price +10.4% above 200d mean; the -4.9% weekly dip looks like a pullback in trend—invalidated below ~237 (50d area).
Impressive 12w relative strength (+24.9%) but 4w rel strength has turned negative (-1.1%) and RSI 46 suggests fading momentum; need to see it hold above ~225 to turn constructive.

Massive 26w gain (+94.2%) and well above 200d mean (+26.8%) but 12w relative strength is only +1.9% and ATR is a wide 3.2%, suggesting the easy money is made; watching for a pullback to the 50d (~179).
Weakest name: RSI 35.7, -7.6% below 200d mean, -16.7% drawdown, negative relative strength on all timeframes; would reconsider only on a sustained close above the 200-day (~162).
RSI 40.1, -4.1% below 50d mean, -7.3% 12w relative strength, and -10.6% drawdown signal a deteriorating trend; needs to reclaim ~225 to neutralize.
Flat trend (only +1.0% above 200d), negative 12w relative strength (-4.8%), and -10.8% drawdown—no reason to own until it breaks above ~123 (52w high area).
Sharp 12w bounce (+23.1%) and strong recent relative strength, but still -43.3% from highs and -11.0% below 200d mean—a bear-market rally until proven otherwise; watching ~315 as support.

memos.headline: S10 and S04 Lead on Earnings Power; S09 and S02 Flash Cash-Flow Compression Warnings
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe between durable, high-margin growers and names where earnings are compressing despite scale. S10 stands out with 56.5% net margin, +55.6% YoY revenue growth, and only $8.47B in total debt—an extraordinary combination. S04 posted 35.6% net margin on $76.44B revenue with +18.1% top-line growth and +23.6% net income growth, confirming durable earnings power. On the other end, S09 saw revenue decline 12.4% YoY with net income down 23.4% and an 8.7% margin, while S02 grew revenue 12.9% but net income fell 19.2%, leaving a razor-thin 3.1% margin against $79.19B in debt—classic cash-flow compression I refuse to pay for. I would need to see margin stabilization in S09 and S02 before reconsidering.

views.note: 56.5% net margin, +55.6% YoY revenue growth, and minimal debt of $8.47B make this the strongest earnings-power story in the universe.
35.6% net margin with +18.1% revenue growth and +23.6% net income growth on a full-year 10-K confirms durable, expanding profitability.
29.2% net margin, +13.8% revenue growth, +19.4% net income growth, and low debt of $14.79B support a clean earnings profile.
Revenue of $167.70B grew 13.3% YoY with net income up 34.7%, showing strong operating leverage despite a modest 10.8% margin; margin expansion trajectory is key to watch.
24.9% net margin is solid but revenue growth of 9.6% is decelerating and $91.80B in total debt is the highest in the universe ex-S06; need to see leverage come down.
17.3% net margin and +15.3% net income growth are respectable, but only +1.7% revenue growth and $30.37B debt on $20.89B revenue signal limited top-line momentum.
Revenue fell 10.5% YoY, net income dropped 17.4%, and $419.80B in total debt dwarfs the rest of the universe—earnings trajectory is negative.
Revenue down 12.4% YoY with net income down 23.4% and an 8.7% margin signals clear cash-flow compression; would need margin stabilization to reconsider.
Despite +12.9% revenue growth, net income fell 19.2% to a 3.1% margin against $79.19B in debt—textbook margin compression I will not pay for.
Revenue flat at -0.7% YoY, net income down 18.7%, and $31.74B debt on $16.57B revenue; earnings power is eroding.

memos.headline: Fed in Easing Regime with Softening Labor Market; Favor Duration-Sensitive Growth, Lean Against Cyclicals
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in an easing cycle: the upper bound has dropped 75bp over the past year to 4.25%, with another 25bp cut in the last three months. Unemployment has risen 30bp over three months to 4.40%, signaling a cooling labor market, while headline CPI is running at 2.9% y/y—still above target but not accelerating dangerously (only +0.8% over the last three months, roughly 3.2% annualized). The 10y yield has fallen 30bp over three months to 4.05% and the 10y-2y spread has normalized to +54bp, confirming the market is pricing continued easing. This regime—falling rates, softening growth, contained but sticky inflation—favors duration-sensitive growth and defensive staples over cyclicals and banks; a re-acceleration in CPI above 3.5% y/y or a surprise drop in unemployment below 4.0% would force me to revisit.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth benefits most from falling yields and continued Fed easing, with 10y down 30bp in 3 months.
Defensive staples should outperform as unemployment rises and the growth outlook softens.
Banks face a mixed setup: a positively sloped curve helps NIMs but the easing cycle compresses front-end rates and rising unemployment raises credit risk.
Cyclicals are vulnerable as the labor market softens and the Fed is cutting because growth is slowing, not because inflation is vanquished.
Energy tends to underperform in a slowdown regime with rising unemployment and moderating demand expectations.
Another duration-sensitive sector that should benefit as the 10y yield trends lower in an easing cycle.

memos.headline: Limited Sentiment Signals Across Universe; S07 Debt Event and S04 Leadership Change Stand Out
memos.body: I see a thin evidence set this cycle with no GDELT tone data to parse, so I am relying on 8-K filing cadence and event types as proxies for narrative shifts. S07 drew two filings in quick succession—an Other Events disclosure on 8/28 followed by a material definitive agreement creating a direct financial obligation on 9/3—which suggests a new debt issuance or credit facility that could shift sentiment negatively if leverage concerns surface. S04's director departure/appointment on 9/30 is a governance event that can cut either way but often generates brief negative media tone before stabilizing. S02 has been unusually active with three Reg FD filings in three weeks (8/20, 9/8, 9/9 amendment), signaling management is proactively shaping the narrative—typically a mildly positive tone driver. S10's earnings-related 8-K on 8/27 produced a modest -0.8% price reaction, suggesting the market digested the news without panic, and any negative tone is likely already priced.

views.note: Back-to-back filings including a new direct financial obligation may catalyze negative sentiment around leverage.
Director change is a governance event with ambiguous sentiment implications; too early to take a directional view.
Three Reg FD disclosures in rapid succession suggest management is actively engaging investors, a mild positive tone signal.
Earnings 8-K drew only a -0.8% move, indicating negative tone is already absorbed; no fresh catalyst.
Single Reg FD filing on 10/6 provides minimal information to gauge a sentiment shift.
Two Other Events filings in early September lack detail to infer a clear tone direction.
Bylaw amendment is routine governance housekeeping with negligible sentiment impact.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Surges 61% in One Month While Oil Weakness Signals Demand-Side Geopolitical Risk
memos.body: I am flagging a sharp deterioration in the policy environment: the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index hit 391.93 on Oct 9, up 61% month-over-month and 45% over three months, the steepest ramp I have seen in this cycle. VIX has risen 9.2% over the past month to 16.43, confirming that markets are beginning to price the uncertainty, though high-yield spreads at 2.95% remain remarkably tight, suggesting credit markets have not yet capitulated. WTI crude at $62.36 is down over 10% in three months, which I read as a demand-side signal consistent with trade-policy headwinds rather than a supply glut—this matters for energy-exposed names. Without granular detail on the 8-K filings for S02, S05, S07, and S09, I am treating their Reg FD and Other Events disclosures as potential early indicators of supply-chain or regulatory repositioning, and I weight the macro backdrop heavily in my views.

views.note: Three Reg FD filings in quick succession suggest management is actively communicating with investors amid rising policy uncertainty, but without content detail I cannot take a directional view.
Back-to-back 8-K Other Events filings in early September could reflect geopolitical repositioning, but absent specifics I stay neutral with the elevated policy uncertainty backdrop.
Single 8.01 filing in late August provides no actionable geopolitical signal; holding neutral until policy clarity improves.
Recent Oct 6 Reg FD disclosure amid the sharpest policy-uncertainty spike in months warrants monitoring; I would turn constructive only if the filing reveals insulation from trade-policy risk.

With no company-specific filings and the policy uncertainty index at 392, names lacking visible geopolitical hedging or disclosure deserve a cautious stance; a reversal in the EPU trend would change my view.
WTI down 10% in three months and policy uncertainty surging suggest headwinds for names with energy or trade-exposed supply chains; no offsetting company disclosure available.
